subject: Literature
title: Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels
description: A fast breakdown of Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels for builders.

hook.text: Gulliver's Travels is shelved with children's books, but it is actually one of the most savage satires ever written.

buildup.text: Swift sent Gulliver to lands of tiny people, giants, flying islands, and rational horses to expose human absurdity.

discovery.text: In the final voyage, intelligent horses view humans as disgusting animals, and Gulliver comes to agree with them.

twist.text: Swift was not writing fantasy for children. He was attacking the British Empire, the Royal Society, and human nature.

climax.text: Gulliver's Travels invented dystopian satire: using imaginary societies to reveal the horrors within our own.

punchline.text: A children's adventure story was actually a scream of rage.

quiz.question: What was Swift actually attacking through Gulliver's Travels?
options: Only the travel writing genre of his era
The British Empire, the Royal Society, and human nature itself
